newsitem.title: POLAND: Unions threaten strike at Poland's Gdansk refinery.
newsitem.headline: Unions threaten strike at Poland's Gdansk refinery.

text.p: Unions at Poland's Rafineria Gdanska SA oil refinery will ballot the workforce on calling a strike in protest over delays in giving employees shares in the enterprise, the unions said in a statement on Tuesday.

"In connection with the fact that shares were not conveyed to employees of Rafineria Gdanska SA by December 31, 1996, the trade unions operating at the refinery have begun a collective dispute with the management...and are organising a referendum aimed at calling a strike," the statement said.
The vote, organised by four unions, should be completed by the end of January and a decision to strike could be made then.

The refinery has been transformed into a state treasury controlled joint stock company as a prelude to its privatisation and by law employees should get up to 15 percent of shares in such companies for free.
The refinery, Poland's second largest, processed 2.86 million tonnes of crude oil in 1995. Its net profit was 125.1 million zlotys on sales revenue of 2.77 billion zlotys.
The plant, in the Baltic port city Gdansk, employs 1,800 people.
